parsed.study_design: Qualitative socio-legal document study using methodological triangulation, legal hermeneutics, case-law analysis, and adapted Global Integrity indicators
parsed.population_and_sample: Water-service users and consumers in Argentina, focusing on the national jurisdiction and Province of Buenos Aires; documentary sample includes applicable legislation, regulatory institutions, administrative remedies, and selected Argentine judicial cases from 1993 onward.
parsed.exposure: Consumer-protection laws, water-service regulation, regulatory-agency arrangements, complaint mechanisms, judicial remedies, and institutional overlap among water-control bodies.
parsed.outcome: Protection against water disconnection for nonpayment, sewerage billing relief, availability of complaint and redress mechanisms, regulatory enforcement, service coverage, affordability, and effective exercise of water-service access rights.
parsed.rationale: The Methods section (pp. 7–8) identifies a triangulated socio-legal design examining legislation, official statistics, judicial sources, public materials, and adapted Global Integrity indicators. The case-law section (p. 12) reports concrete access outcomes, including orders preventing interruption or reduction of potable-water service and relief from sewerage charges, while the results and conclusions (pp. 16–19) assess regulatory enforcement, institutional overlap, complaint mechanisms, coverage, and affordability. Spanish translation is feasible from the supplied full text.
